items.title: Screening and support are confused in the literature
items.whyItMatters: Studies of support for identified caregivers (claim c2) do not show that screening everyone helps.
items.opportunity: Classify every included study by what was compared: screening plus referral, support alone, or tool accuracy.

items.title: Only one study tested screening itself
items.whyItMatters: The clinic's decision rests on the least-studied link.
items.opportunity: Search specifically for screening-versus-no-screening comparisons, including grey literature.

items.title: Some caregivers are rarely screened
items.whyItMatters: Adult children and caregivers with limited English were missed (claim c3).
items.opportunity: Extract results by relationship, gender and language.

items.title: Referral uptake is low
items.whyItMatters: Most referred caregivers never reached support (claim c4).
items.opportunity: Treat referral uptake as a review outcome.

errorsFound: A claim that screening reduces care home admission by a third is circulating; no retrieved record reports it.
reevaluation: The review is worth doing if it separates screening from support and reports equity and uptake.
summary: Four gaps: confusion of screening and support, one direct study, missed caregivers, and low uptake.
